title: Comparison, Change & Choosing
description: より〜のほうが, いちばん, なる (become), にする (decide on), and turning verbs into nouns with の (のが好き/上手/下手).

points.title: より〜のほうが: is more … than
points.summary: AよりBのほうが〜 = 'B is more … than A'. より marks the loser and のほうが the winner. Ask with AとBと、どちらが〜.
points.body:
Japanese adjectives don't change for comparison (there's no 'bigger'). Instead you mark the items:
- **より** = 'than'. It marks the thing compared against.
- **のほうが** = 'the side of …'. It marks the one that 'wins'.

The full pattern is **AよりBのほうが[adjective]**: 電車よりバスのほうが安いです (the bus is cheaper than the train). Either part can stand alone: バスのほうが安いです / バスは電車より安いです.

**Asking:** AとBと、**どちらが**〜ですか. Answer with Bのほうが〜です. (Never どちらは.)

**Mistakes to avoid:**
- Don't add もっと just to make a comparative. より already does that job (もっと is only for emphasis).
- ほうが needs の after nouns (バスのほう), but not after verbs (歩くほうが).
examples: {東京|とうきょう}は{大阪|おおさか}より{大|おお}きいです。
Tokyo is bigger than Osaka.
{犬|いぬ}と{猫|ねこ}と、どちらが{好|す}きですか。—{猫|ねこ}のほうが{好|す}きです。
Which do you like better, dogs or cats? — I prefer cats.
{電車|でんしゃ}よりバスのほうが{安|やす}いです。
The bus is cheaper than the train.

points.title: いちばん: the most
points.summary: いちばん + adjective = superlative. The group is marked with 〜の中で or 〜で. Ask with 何/だれ/どこ/いつ が いちばん〜.
points.body:
**いちばん** (一番, literally 'number one') goes right before the adjective to make a superlative: いちばん高い (the tallest), いちばん好き (favourite).

The **group** being compared is marked with **〜の中で** or **〜で**:
- 果物**の中で**、りんごが**いちばん**好きです。
- クラス**で**いちばん背が高い人。

**Asking:** use a question word + **が**: 何**が**いちばん好きですか, だれ**が**いちばん速いですか.
For comparing exactly two things, use どちら/〜のほうが, not いちばん.
examples: {果物|くだもの}の{中|なか}で、{何|なに}がいちばん{好|す}きですか。
Among fruits, which do you like best?
{家族|かぞく}でいちばん{背|せ}が{高|たか}いのは{父|ちち}です。
The tallest person in my family is my father.

points.title: なる: to become
points.summary: Noun/な-adjective + に + なる; い-adjective (drop い) + く + なる. It describes a change.
points.body:
**なる** describes a change of state:
- **Noun + になる**: 医者**に**なる, 20歳**に**なる, 春**に**なる
- **な-adjective + になる**: 元気**に**なる, 上手**に**なる, きれい**に**なる
- **い-adjective → 〜くなる**: 寒い → 寒**く**なる, 大きい → 大き**く**なる (いい → **よく**なる)

Past tense なりました is very common for 'has become / got': 暖かくなりましたね (it's got warmer, hasn't it).

**Watch out:** きれい, 嫌い and 有名 are な-adjectives even though some end in い, so it's きれい**に**なる, not きれくなる.
examples: {春|はる}になって、{暖|あたた}かくなりました。
Spring has come and it's got warmer.
{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}になりましたね。
Your Japanese has really improved.
{将来|しょうらい}、{医者|いしゃ}になりたいです。
I want to become a doctor in the future.

points.title: にする: to decide on, to choose
points.summary: Noun + にする = 'I'll have / go with …'. A decision or choice made by you (vs. になる, a change that just happens).
points.body:
**Noun + にする** expresses a **choice or decision**:
- At a restaurant: 私はカレー**にします** (I'll have the curry).
- Planning: 旅行は来月**にしましょう** (let's make the trip next month).
- Asking: 何**にします**か (what will you have?).

**にする vs になる:**
- **にする**: someone actively chooses or makes it so.
- **になる**: it changes or turns out that way by itself.

With verbs, the pattern becomes **ことにする** ('decide to do'), which is N4: 毎日走ることにしました.

Related: adjectives + する mean 'make something …': 部屋をきれい**にする** (make the room tidy), 音を小さ**くする** (turn the volume down).
examples: わたしはコーヒーにします。
I'll have coffee.
{会議|かいぎ}は{月曜日|げつようび}にしましょう。
Let's set the meeting for Monday.
{部屋|へや}をきれいにしてください。
Please tidy up the room.

points.title: の (2): turning a verb phrase into a noun
points.summary: Plain verb + の = 'the act of doing'. It lets a verb phrase work as a subject or object: 読むのが好き, 話すのは難しい.
points.body:
Particles (が, を, は) need a **noun** in front of them. To talk about an **action** as a thing, put **の** after the plain form of the verb:
- 本を読む**の**が好きです (I like reading books).
- 日本語を話す**の**は難しいです (speaking Japanese is hard).
- 宿題をする**の**を忘れました (I forgot to do my homework).

**こと** can often replace の here (読むことが好き). こと sounds more abstract or formal, の more immediate. A few patterns need one or the other: ことができる (can do) always uses こと, while perception verbs like 見る and 聞く take の.
examples: {本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのが{好|す}きです。
I like reading books.
{漢字|かんじ}を{覚|おぼ}えるのは{大変|たいへん}です。
Memorising kanji is tough.
{電気|でんき}を{消|け}すのを{忘|わす}れました。
I forgot to turn off the light.

points.title: のが好き / のが上手 / のが下手: like / be good / be bad at doing
points.summary: Verb + のが + 好き/嫌い/上手/下手 talks about activities you like or are good or bad at. Always が, never を.
points.body:
These combine **の (nominalizer)** with adjectives that take **が**:
- 歌う**のが好き**です: I like singing.
- 料理をする**のが上手**です: (she) is good at cooking.
- 絵をかく**のが下手**です: I'm bad at drawing.
- 早く起きる**のが嫌い**です: I hate getting up early.

**Grammar notes:**
- The particle is **が** because 好き, 上手 and 下手 are adjectives, not action verbs. のを好き is wrong.
- The topic (the person) takes は: 姉**は**歌うの**が**上手です.
- Modest usage: 上手 is a compliment for **others**. About yourself, Japanese people prefer 得意 (N4) or understate.
examples: {姉|あね}は{歌|うた}を{歌|うた}うのが{上手|じょうず}です。
My older sister is good at singing.
わたしは{料理|りょうり}をするのが{下手|へた}です。
I'm bad at cooking.
{旅行|りょこう}するのが{大好|だいす}きです。
I love travelling.

questions.prompt: {犬|いぬ}（　）{猫|ねこ}のほうが{好|す}きです。
questions.explanation: **AよりBのほうが** = 'B more than A'. より marks the item compared against.
notes: Nouns take より directly: 犬より, not 犬のより.
ほう is already used with 猫. 犬ほう猫のほう is ungrammatical.
ほど is used with negatives (犬ほど好きじゃない).
questions.translation: I like cats more than dogs.

questions.prompt: A：{夏|なつ}と{冬|ふゆ}と、どちらが{好|す}きですか。　B：{夏|なつ}の（　）が{好|す}きです。
questions.explanation: Answer a どちら question with **〜のほうが**.
notes: 夏のものが would mean 'summer things'.
夏のよりが isn't a form. より directly follows the noun (夏より).
どちら is the question word, so the answer can't contain it.
questions.translation: A: Which do you like better, summer or winter? B: I prefer summer.

questions.prompt: {電車|でんしゃ}とバスと、（　）が{速|はや}いですか。
questions.explanation: Comparing **two** things: **どちら**.
notes: どこ asks 'where?'.
どれ is for choosing among three or more.
どの must be followed by a noun (どの乗り物).
questions.translation: Which is faster, the train or the bus?

questions.prompt: {新幹線|しんかんせん}は{飛行機|ひこうき}より（　）。
questions.explanation: With より, the adjective stays in its **normal form**. Japanese has no special comparative.
notes: のほう attaches to the winning noun (新幹線のほうが), not to the adjective.
より is already used. 遅いよりです is ungrammatical.
もっと遅くです isn't grammatical. 遅く can't take です.
questions.translation: The Shinkansen is slower than a plane.

questions.prompt: {家族|かぞく}の{中|なか}で、{父|ちち}が（　）{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
questions.explanation: Within a group (の中で), 'the most' is **いちばん**.
notes: ほど is used with negatives (父ほど高くない).
より needs a noun before it ('than X').
もっと means 'more' and is for comparing two things, not ranking in a group.
questions.translation: In my family, my father is the tallest.

questions.prompt: スポーツ（　）{何|なに}がいちばん{好|す}きですか。
questions.explanation: The group for いちばん takes **で** (or の中で).
notes: に doesn't mark the comparison group.
と would mean 'together with sports'.
を would make sports an object.
questions.translation: Which sport do you like most?

questions.prompt: {一年|いちねん}で（　）がいちばん{寒|さむ}いですか。
questions.explanation: Asking for a time within the year: **いつ**が. (何月が would also work.)
notes: どの must be followed by a noun (どの月).
いくつ asks 'how many / how old'.
どちら is for choosing between two options.
questions.translation: When is it coldest in the year?

questions.prompt: {四月|しがつ}になって、{暖|あたた}か（　）なりました。
questions.explanation: い-adjective → drop い + **く** + なる.
notes: になる is for nouns and な-adjectives.
で is the connective form of な-adjectives.
な is for modifying nouns.
questions.translation: It's April and it's got warmer.

questions.prompt: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}して、{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}（　）なりました。
questions.explanation: 上手 is a な-adjective, so **に** + なる.
notes: 上手く (うまく) is a different word. 上手 (じょうず) is a な-adjective and takes に.
な is used before nouns.
が can't come between an adjective and なる.
questions.translation: I practised every day and my Japanese got better.

questions.prompt: {来月|らいげつ}、20{歳|さい}（　）なります。
questions.explanation: Noun + **に** + なる.
notes: 20歳でなります isn't grammatical. 20歳で means 'at age 20'.
く is for い-adjectives.
が would make '20 years old' the subject that becomes something.
questions.translation: I'll turn 20 next month.

questions.prompt: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んで、{風邪|かぜ}が（　）なりました。
questions.explanation: いい is irregular: its く-form is **よく** (from よい).
notes: いい is an い-adjective, so に is wrong.
いく isn't a form of いい.
よい is an い-adjective too, so it's よく, not よいに.
questions.translation: I took medicine and my cold got better.

questions.prompt: （At a restaurant）{店員|てんいん}：ご{注文|ちゅうもん}は？　{客|きゃく}：カレー（　）します。
questions.explanation: Choosing something: noun + **にします** ('I'll have …').
notes: が would make the curry the one doing.
で would mean 'by means of curry'.
カレーをします means 'do curry', which doesn't mean ordering it.
questions.translation: Waiter: Your order? Customer: I'll have the curry.

questions.prompt: {旅行|りょこう}は{来月|らいげつ}に（　）。
questions.explanation: Deciding on a time: **にする** → にしましょう ('let's make it next month').
notes: しりましょう isn't a form of する.
なる describes an unplanned change. You can't suggest 'let's become next month'.
ましょう attaches to the ます-stem し, not the dictionary form.
questions.translation: Let's make the trip next month.

questions.prompt: {寒|さむ}いですね。エアコンの{温度|おんど}を{高|たか}（　）しましょうか。
questions.explanation: 'Make something …' with an い-adjective: drop い + **く** + する.
notes: な is for modifying nouns.
で doesn't combine with する like this.
に + する is for nouns and な-adjectives (静かにする).
questions.translation: It's cold, isn't it? Shall I turn the air conditioner up?

questions.prompt: {日本語|にほんご}を{話|はな}す（　）は{難|むずか}しいです。
questions.explanation: Verb + **の** turns 'speaking Japanese' into a noun that can take は.
notes: のがは doubles the particles. は replaces が.
のをは isn't possible.
話すでは isn't the nominalizing structure.
questions.translation: Speaking Japanese is difficult.

questions.prompt: {電気|でんき}を{消|け}す（　）を{忘|わす}れました。
questions.explanation: Verb + **の** + を: 'forgot (the act of) turning off'.
notes: のに means 'even though / for', and のにを isn't possible.
ので means 'because', and のでを isn't possible.
のがを doubles the particles.
questions.translation: I forgot to turn off the light.

questions.prompt: {子供|こども}が{公園|こうえん}で{遊|あそ}んでいる（　）が{見|み}えます。
questions.explanation: With perception verbs (見える, 聞こえる, 見る), the nominalizer must be **の**, not こと.
notes: こと can't be used with perception verbs. You see a scene, not an abstract fact.
もの refers to objects, not an action you see.
ところにが isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: I can see children playing in the park.

questions.prompt: {姉|あね}は{歌|うた}を{歌|うた}うのが（　）です。
questions.explanation: **のが上手です** = 'is good at'. Before です, the な-adjective stands alone.
notes: な is only used before a noun.
上手 is a な-adjective, so it doesn't take く.
上手にです isn't a form. に makes an adverb.
questions.translation: My older sister is good at singing.

questions.prompt: わたしは{料理|りょうり}をするの（　）{好|す}きです。
questions.explanation: 好き takes **が**, also after verb + の.
notes: に doesn't mark what you like.
で doesn't mark what you like.
のを好き is a classic mistake. 好き is an adjective, not a verb.
questions.translation: I like cooking.

questions.prompt: {絵|え}をかくのが（　）なので、{練習|れんしゅう}しています。
questions.explanation: Practising because you're **bad** at it: **下手**.
notes: に makes an adverb and can't come before なので.
上手 ('good at') doesn't explain why you'd need to practise.
な is only used before a noun. Before なので, use the bare stem: 下手なので (the な there belongs to ので).
questions.translation: I'm bad at drawing, so I'm practising.

questions.prompt: バスより{歩|ある}く（　）が{健康|けんこう}にいいです。
questions.explanation: Verb + **ほうが** (no の).
notes: After a verb, ほう attaches directly — の is only after nouns (バスのほう).
ほどが isn't the comparison pattern.
より is already used for the other side.
questions.translation: Walking is better for your health than the bus.

questions.prompt: {三人|さんにん}の{中|なか}（　）、だれがいちばん{背|せ}が{高|たか}いですか。
questions.explanation: Comparison group: **〜の中で**.
notes: の中に is for 'inside something'; the comparison group takes で.
を marks objects.
が would make the group the subject.
questions.translation: Who is the tallest of the three?

questions.prompt: {外|そと}が{暗|くら}く（　）から、{帰|かえ}りましょう。
questions.explanation: 暗い → 暗く + **なった** (became dark).
notes: た can't attach to the dictionary form.
なっだ isn't a form — る-verbs end in った.
The past of なる is なった — not built from the ます-stem.
questions.translation: It's got dark outside, so let's go home.

questions.prompt: {飲|の}み{物|もの}は{何|なに}（　）しますか。
questions.explanation: Choosing: **〜にする** → 何にしますか.
notes: 何をしますか = 'what will you do?' — doesn't ask for a choice of drink.
何がしますか isn't grammatical.
何でしますか isn't the choice pattern.
questions.translation: What will you have to drink?

questions.prompt: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}く（　）が{好|す}きです。
questions.explanation: Verb + **の** + が好き.
notes: のに means 'for / even though' — not a nominalizer here.
のをが doubles particles.
ので means 'because'.
questions.translation: I like listening to music.

questions.prompt: {兄|あに}は{泳|およ}ぐ（　）が{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.explanation: Verb + **のが上手**.
notes: 泳ぐもの = 'things that swim'.
ので means 'because'.
のをが doubles particles.
questions.translation: My older brother is good at swimming.
